headline.label: Share of jail population awaiting trial, 2019

sections.heading: Local jails grew even as state prisons leveled off
paragraphs: Between 2000 and 2019, the average daily jail population nationwide rose 19.4%, from 613,162 to 732,033 people. Over the same period, the state and federal prison population grew far more slowly, 7.2%, from 981,582 to 1,052,607.
The story of incarceration growth in this century is increasingly a story about county jails, not state prisons.

sections.heading: A stark racial gap in who is jailed
paragraphs: In 2019, Black adults were jailed at a rate of 822 per 100,000, more than three times the White rate of 265 per 100,000. Native American adults were also jailed at an elevated rate of 575 per 100,000, while Latinx adults were jailed at the same rate as White adults (262 per 100,000), and AAPI adults were jailed at a much lower rate of 41 per 100,000.
These rates are per 100,000 adults age 15-64 of each group, not raw counts, so they are directly comparable across groups of very different sizes.

sections.heading: The Black-white jail gap has narrowed, but slowly
paragraphs: The ratio between Black and White jail incarceration rates fell from 5.56× in 2000 to 3.11× in 2019. The gap has closed steadily over two decades, but Black adults were still jailed at more than three times the White rate as of the most recent complete year.

sections.heading: Rural counties jail people at more than double the urban rate
paragraphs: In 2019, rural counties jailed people at a rate of 581 per 100,000 adults, more than double the urban rate of 271 per 100,000. Small and mid-sized counties sat in between at 415 per 100,000, while suburban counties had the lowest rate of the four, 267 per 100,000.
This pattern is well documented in criminal justice research: rural areas tend to have fewer pretrial services and diversion alternatives, so jail is used more often as a default.

sections.heading: Geography matters: the South jails at twice the Northeast's rate
paragraphs: In 2019, the South had a jail incarceration rate of 476 per 100,000 adults, roughly double the Northeast's rate of 232 per 100,000. The West (295) and Midwest (285) fell in between.

sections.heading: Most people sitting in jail haven't been convicted of anything
paragraphs: The share of the jail population held pretrial, meaning charged but not yet convicted, rose from 54.7% in 2000 to 63.3% in 2019. By the most recent complete year, nearly two out of every three people in jail on a given day were legally presumed innocent.

sections.heading: Women are a small but fast-growing share of the jail population
paragraphs: Women made up 11.8% of the jail population in 2000, rising to 14.5% by 2019. Men remain the large majority of people in jail, but the female share has grown in nearly every year of the last two decades.

sections.heading: Nearly a quarter of counties are jailing more people than their jails are built for
paragraphs: Comparing 2019 jail populations to each jail's rated capacity, 23.0% of the 2,796 counties reporting a rated capacity exceeded it, and the national average utilization was 88.4% of rated capacity.

sections.heading: A handful of counties post incarceration rates far above the national average
paragraphs: The national incarceration rate (jail plus prison) was about 797 per 100,000 adults in 2019. Among counties with at least 50,000 working-age adults, the highest rate was in Bowie County, TX at 3787 per 100,000, more than 5 times the national rate.
